checks.//: ═══ FLEET HEALTH — every pack carries these, so the pack runs on its own. None needs crop tuning. ═══

FRUIT FREEZE. UC: round oranges begin to take fruit damage after 4 h at −2.2 °C (28 °F); mandarin fruit tolerates a brief −4.4 °C but begins to freeze after several hours at −3.3 °C. Eureka lemon and grapefruit are the most sensitive, but no UC source gives a lemon figure — for lemon blocks, raise max rather than trusting this one. Wood damage after 4 h: orange −4.4 °C, Meyer lemon −5.6 °C, mandarin −6.7 °C. Sources: UC IPM, "Frost protection for citrus", https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/GARDEN/FRUIT/ENVIRON/citrusfrost.html ; UC Real Dirt, https://ucanr.edu/blog/real-dirt/article/frost-protection-citrus-1

START WIND MACHINES. FAO Frost Protection (Snyder, UC Davis): start at about 0 °C, and before the crop's critical temperature; lemon groves start 1–2 °C higher than oranges. Machines only help under an inversion, and should not run without one when the wet-bulb temperature is below −2.2 °C. Keep running for hours after sunrise after a damaging night. Sources: FAO, https://www.fao.org/4/y7223e/y7223e0d.htm ; Ventura UCCE, https://ucanr.edu/county/cooperative-extension-ventura-county/frost-control/freeze-damage

FROST TONIGHT. FAO Frost Protection (Snyder, UC Davis): start wind machines at about 0 °C, and in any case before the crop's critical temperature. Raised up to 14 h ahead so the decision is made the evening before. DISABLED: needs the top-level forecast block and a Weatherbit key (see README, Forecast).

═══ SOIL ═══ June drop (late May–early July) is increased by sudden heat at or after fruit set, but UC gives no temperature, so there is no heat check here. Source: UC IPM, "Fruit drop of citrus", https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/fruit-drop-of-citrus/

ROOT-ZONE SALINITY — orange (Maas & Grattan 1999; FAO 29 lists 1.7): Maas–Hoffman threshold ECe 1.3 dS/m, above which yield declines. DISABLED until converted to what the probe reads. Maas–Hoffman thresholds are saturated-paste ECe. A soil probe reports bulk EC (or pore EC), which is not ECe: FAO 29 gives soil-water EC ≈ 2 × ECe at field capacity, and bulk EC is lower than pore EC and moves with water content. Convert before enabling — take a saturated-paste lab sample beside the probe and scale this threshold by the probe/ECe ratio. Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, ch. 2 and Annex 1 (Maas & Grattan 1999), https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e02.htm , https://www.fao.org/4/y4263e/y4263e0e.htm

ROOT-ZONE SALINITY — lemon: Maas–Hoffman threshold ECe 1.5 dS/m, above which yield declines. DISABLED until converted to what the probe reads. Maas–Hoffman thresholds are saturated-paste ECe. A soil probe reports bulk EC (or pore EC), which is not ECe: FAO 29 gives soil-water EC ≈ 2 × ECe at field capacity, and bulk EC is lower than pore EC and moves with water content. Convert before enabling — take a saturated-paste lab sample beside the probe and scale this threshold by the probe/ECe ratio. Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, ch. 2 and Annex 1 (Maas & Grattan 1999), https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e02.htm , https://www.fao.org/4/y4263e/y4263e0e.htm

SOIL pH — citrus: outside 6.0–7.5. UF/IFAS: "The optimum soil pH range for citrus is 6.0 to 6.5", and deficiencies are more likely outside it; high pH reduces Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn and Mn availability, and Swingle citrumelo grows poorly on high-pH soil. No UC production figure was found, so the 7.5 ceiling is this pack's choice for California's more alkaline soils (NMSU, general: iron and zinc deficiency above 7.5) — set max to 6.5 to follow UF/IFAS exactly, or on Swingle rootstock. pH moves over seasons, not hours, so this is info and needs a day sustained. Sources: UF/IFAS SL456, https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/SS669 ; UF/IFAS SL458, https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/SS671 ; NMSU CR-676, https://pubs.nmsu.edu/_circulars/CR676/index.html
